header-title.purpose: The hub's name in the header bar and over the sign-in form. Uppercase with 0.1em tracking in the dark theme; as written with 0.02em in Workshop's header.

headline.purpose: An app's name on its tile, a page heading, the heading of a no-access card or an error (Friz Quadrata).

title.purpose: A section heading on a page and a dialog's title (Friz Quadrata).

body.purpose: Everything read as a sentence: dialog text, log entries, menu items. An error block stops at 62ch.

body-strong.purpose: A line's title, a person's name, button labels, tabs and toasts.

field.purpose: Text in fields on phones and touch screens, and in every field the core draws.

meta.purpose: Roles, sub-lines, chips, hints, error lines and addresses.

meta-strong.purpose: The label of a small button.

meta-figures.purpose: Dates and ages, in tabular figures.

label.purpose: Uppercase, in Muted Ash: a field's caption, a column head, the label over a tile's lines. It names what is directly under it and never sits over a heading.

count.purpose: The number in a count bubble; tabular figures, no tracking.

mono.purpose: A password or key shown once.

shadows.name: floating-panel
shadows.purpose: Only on layers that float and can be dismissed: dialogs, menus, toasts, the app switcher. Workshop theme: 0 12px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, .18).

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Behind a dialog, and behind the switcher when it is a sheet on a phone. Workshop theme: rgba(26, 26, 24, .35).

shadows.name: pinned-column-rule
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the 1px Rule Grey line on the inner edge of the pinned person column, drawn as an inset.

shadows.name: workshop-count-edge
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the 1px edge the hub's stylesheet gives the count bubble in Workshop, in the count's own colour. Open question with the owner; not a pattern for new components.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The family ease-out. Everything that moves uses it.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: A button changing colour; a menu rising 6px and fading in.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: A dialog rising 6px and fading in; a toast rising 8px and fading in; the sheet's scrim fading in.

motion.name: switcher-pop
motion.purpose: The core only: the app switcher growing from 96% and fading in from under its button. A plain number in the core, not a family token.

motion.name: sheet
motion.purpose: The core only: the switcher sliding up as a sheet on a phone. The same value as the family's panel duration, written as a plain number in the core.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: With reduced motion asked for, the family's durations collapse to 0 and the hub's and the core's animations are switched off.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Below: one column of tiles, the tabs on a row of their own, 16px page padding, the pinned person column at 184px, the switcher as a sheet from the bottom.

breakpoints.name: desk
breakpoints.purpose: At or above: only the page padding grows (28px above, 48px at the sides, 32px below). Every screen is also checked at about 900px, half a screen.

breakpoints.name: touch
breakpoints.purpose: A phone by its width or an iPad by its pointer: every control takes its 44px size and fields take 16px text.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled button in a view or dialog (Add person, Sign in). Upsdell Red in the dark theme, Ink in Workshop.

narrative.overview:
The hub is a front door, not a merged system. A signed-in person opens it between other work, at a desk PC and often in a window snapped to half a screen, to step into one of the Stella apps or straight to the thing that is waiting inside one. So each app is one tile, and the tile's face is that app's own overview: where to go and what needs attention are the same object. The whole tile is a door, and each line on it is a smaller door to one thing.

It wears the family's look and owns none of it. The colour, type, spacing and motion tokens are the Stella family's, copied unchanged from a sibling app and fixed. The hub builds its components on those tokens and brings no palette of its own, so a theme changes variables and cannot miss a spot. Dark Stella is the default, and the light Workshop theme is a variable override for bright rooms. The page is greyscale at rest: red is one filled button at most and otherwise a line or a marker, amber marks what is late or wants doing, and nothing casts a shadow unless it floats above the page and will go away.

There are two layers. The hub's own page (the front page, Accounts and the account log) is drawn by `css/hub.css` on the family tokens. The shared core draws a few things inside the other apps' pages: the sign-in screen, the no-access cards, the change-password dialog, the app switcher and a toast. Those pages have stylesheets the hub does not own, so everything the core draws sits under one root element, starts from a clean slate, and carries its own short-named copy of the family tokens. That copy is kept in step by hand.
keyCharacteristics: One tile per app, with that app's overview on its face. The tile is a door, and so is each line on it.
The Stella family's tokens, fixed. Dark by default, light Workshop by variable override.
Greyscale at rest. Red is one filled button at most, and otherwise a line or a marker. Amber marks what is late or wants doing.
Friz Quadrata names places. The body face does every line, label and control.
Flat surfaces told apart by tone and a 1px edge. Shadows only on what floats.
Room is held before content arrives: flat skeletons the size of the lines, no shimmer and no shift.
Built for a desk and a half-screen window first, with 44px targets on phones and touch screens.
Words only where a control needs them: a label, a rule, an error.
A shared core, drawn inside the other apps, with its own hand-kept copy of the tokens.

rules.name: The Family Tokens Rule
rules.body: Every colour, size and curve comes from the family's stylesheet. The hub's own stylesheet names no colour, so a theme overrides variables and cannot miss a spot. The one exception is the white label on a toast. The tokens change only with the owner's approval.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Upsdell Red fills one primary button in a view or dialog, and the toast for something that did not work. Burning Star Red is a line or a marker (the header rule, the current tab, focus, a caret, a destructive outline, a count) and never fills anything larger than a count bubble.

rules.name: The Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means late or wants doing, and nothing else. It always sits on words or figures that say the same thing: a date that has passed, a sentence, a button's label.

rules.name: The Friz-for-Places Rule
rules.body: Friz Quadrata names where you are or what you are being asked: the hub, an app, a page, a section, a dialog. Anything read in a line or pressed is in the body face. A line's title, a button, a tab and a label are never set in Friz.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Dates, ages and counts use tabular figures, so a column of them lines up and does not jitter as it changes.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: On phones and touch screens a field's text is 16px, so iOS never zooms the page on focus. The core's fields are 16px at every width, because the core cannot know the page it is drawn in.

rules.name: The Half-Screen Rule
rules.body: Every screen has to hold at about 900px wide (a window snapped beside CAD) as well as at 390px and 1440px, and the review screenshots are taken at all three. Nothing depends on width above 1100px except the page's padding.

rules.name: The Held Space Rule
rules.body: A tile holds the room for its card from the moment it is drawn: 206px, which is a 36px label and three 56px lines with the two 1px rules between them. The card arrives into exactly that, so the page does not move.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: On a phone or a touch screen everything that can be pressed is at least 44px tall, or is given that much room to be hit. A 22px chip that is a button reaches 11px past its own top and bottom.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing at rest casts a shadow. Tiles, grids, lists and rows are flat. A shadow means "this is above the page and will go away".

rules.name: The Dashed Rule
rules.body: A dashed edge means nothing here, or not yours to change: the empty box, a disabled button, a disabled field. A solid edge is never used for either.

rules.name: The One Stroke Rule
rules.body: Every icon is a 1.8 stroke on a 24 grid with round caps and joins. Dots are the only filled shapes: the three dots of "more", the point of the exclamation mark, and the nine dots of the switcher button.

dos: **Do** build every component on the family variables, in `css/hub.css` or under the core's root, so the Workshop theme cannot miss a spot.
**Do** change the core's copy of a token in the same change as the family's value, in both themes, using the table under The core's copy.
**Do** check every screen at 390px, about 900px and 1440px, on a touch screen, and in both themes.
**Do** hold the room for anything that loads after the page, with flat blocks the size of what they stand for (the Held Space Rule).
**Do** give everything that can be pressed 44px of height on phones and touch screens, or that much room to be hit.
**Do** show focus as the 2px ring in the focus colour, 2px outside the element, or 2px inside where an outer ring would be clipped.
**Do** set dates, ages and counts in tabular figures.
**Do** outline the destructive button in a confirm, and start that confirm with focus on Cancel.
**Do** say what failed in the heading of an error, and offer one way on.
**Do** draw an icon as a 1.8 stroke on a 24 grid in the text colour.
donts: **Don't** change the family tokens in `css/style.css` or `css/themes.css`, or the Friz Quadrata headings, without the owner's approval.
**Don't** ship the licensed font files (Friz Quadrata, Sweet Sans Pro).
**Don't** fill more than one button in a view or dialog with Upsdell Red, and never fill anything larger than a count bubble with Burning Star Red.
**Don't** put a shadow on a tile, a grid, a row or anything else at rest.
**Don't** use amber for anything that is not late or wanting to be done.
**Don't** set a line's title, a button, a tab, a label or a field in Friz Quadrata.
**Don't** animate anything on load, shimmer a skeleton, or let the page move when content arrives.
**Don't** use a Unicode character as an icon.
**Don't** add words a control does not need: no reassurance and no paragraphs of explanation. A confirm may say what will happen in a sentence.
**Don't** put a real name or address in a mock-up, a fixture or an example. Demo content is invented.
